_note: Properties that guides and bloggers name and src/data/hotels.json does not. A shortlist to research, NOT a list to paste into the sheet - see the sheet-is-not-the-market rule. Every row still needs a human decision.
_method: SERP-seeded sources in data/serp/{hotels,hotels-budget,hostels}.txt, fetched by scripts/consensus.mjs, cleaned of section headings and prose fragments, then diffed against the sheet.
_counting: namedBy counts DISTINCT DOMAINS, not pages. A blog with five accommodation pages is one voice; the page names are kept in `sources` for the audit trail.
_hotelsComRule: Guides and bloggers say what is good. Hotels.com says only whether a property exists and is bookable, because one that is not there can never carry an affiliate link. Validator, never a source. The typeahead answers curl with a CAPTCHA, so the checks below are still unchecked and need the browser.
_community: The community tier is the r/FATTravel thread 'Which of London's best hotels are worth the price?' (17 Aug 2026, 35 comments) - the only on-topic London hotel discussion three last30days runs surfaced across Reddit, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Hacker News and GitHub. 14 of the 17 properties named there were already in the sheet, which is the best independent check on the sheet we have run.
_videoPass: The video pass produced almost nothing usable. Hotel videos are single-property reviews, so the property name is in the TITLE rather than the chapters that scripts/video-research.mjs reads - and the titles are clickbait ('I Stayed in Britain's CHEAPEST Capsule Hotel' names nothing). Its one real result was finding Love and London, now a source in its own right.
